released: v1 2024 (exact date unconfirmed); v4 current (leaderboard page last updated 2026-04-12)
org: UC Berkeley (Gorilla project; ICML 2025 paper; author list not verified)
tests: Whether a model can call functions (tools) correctly: single, multiple, parallel and nested calls, multi-turn conversations, web search and memory (v4 agentic part), and not calling a tool when none fits.
questions: v3 multi-turn: 200 base + 600 augmented entries; v4 agentic: 665 entries (web search 200, memory 465) plus 5,200 format-sensitivity entries; total across all categories not stated on pages I fetched
format: Function calling: user request + function schemas in, a function call out (native FC mode or plain-text Prompt mode)
scoring: Overall Accuracy = unweighted average of sub-categories on the leaderboard page; a blog post gives weights Agentic 40%, Multi-Turn 30%, Live/Non-Live/Hallucination 10% each (the two statements conflict; unconfirmed which is current). Single-turn calls are checked by AST matching; multi-turn by backend state plus response path; web search by exact match on the answer field.
best_score: 77.47% on a BenchmarkList table (Claude Opus 4.5 FC, imported from the leaderboard); a different aggregator (BenchLM) lists BTL-3 88.5% (Bad Theory Labs, self-reported). The two disagree; unconfirmed.
saturated_note: Saturation: not saturated; BenchLM says top scores still spread 13.5 points over the top three. Multi-turn is the hard part (top multi-turn 68.38 on one table). Contamination: the page has no contamination note; web-search blog says a few newer models answered some questions without searching, probably from training data. What scores depend on: native FC vs Prompt mode, the exact BFCL code version (leaderboard cites commit f7cf735 and package bfcl-eval 2025.12.17), a DuckDuckGo search tool with injected fetch failures for web search, and the memory backends. Vendor numbers are mostly self-reported (BenchLM: 23 of 24 rows). Qwen3.5 reports use the name BFCL-V4 (Qwen3.5-4B 50.3). Version changes: v1 AST metric, v2 enterprise/OSS functions, v3 multi-turn, v4 holistic agentic.

released: tau-bench 2024-06; tau2-bench 2025-06; tau3 release 2026 (exact date unconfirmed)
org: Sierra (tau-bench: Yao, Shinn, Razavi, Narasimhan; tau2: Barres, Dong, Ray, Si, Narasimhan; affiliations from the GitHub/site, not the arXiv pages)
tests: An AI customer-service agent talks to a simulated user, calls domain tools (APIs) and must follow a written policy. Domains: retail and airline (tau-bench); telecom added with dual control, where the user also acts on the world (tau2); banking knowledge, voice (tau3).
questions: tau-bench: 115 retail + 50 airline tasks (paper Table 1); tau2 and tau3 task counts not stated on pages I fetched
format: Multi-turn conversation: user simulator (an LLM) + agent with tools + policy document; tau2 telecom adds user-side tools
scoring: pass^k: chance that all k repeated trials of a task succeed (consistency); success means the final database state equals the annotated goal state. pass^1 is the usual headline.
best_score: 99.1% on BenchLM's display-only tau2 table (GLM-5.2, Artificial Analysis telecom run; aggregator, mostly secondary reports); on taubench.com, text tau2: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B 87.9% pass^1
saturated_note: Saturation: near on the telecom domain in aggregator tables (top three within 0.3 points, BenchLM calls it saturated), but BenchLM says rows are not comparable. Original tau-bench was broken: an audit (arXiv 2605.08545) found errors in 25 of 50 airline tasks and pass^5 doubled (20.8% to 40.0%) after excluding them; SABER also reports annotation errors; Sierra fixed 50+ airline and retail tasks in 2026-02 and made 75+ fixes in tau3. Contamination: not discussed in the sources I read. What scores depend on: the user-simulator model (original paper used gpt-4-0613 at temperature 1.0; the repo example uses gpt-4.1; Qwen3.5 and GLM-5 do not name theirs), the task version (before/after fixes), the airline fixes from the Claude Opus 4.5 system card that Qwen3.5 and GLM-5 both apply, the prompt tweaks GLM-5 added for retail and telecom, and which domain or average is reported. tau3 grading update 2026-07 changed only banking_knowledge scores. Initial finding: gpt-4o under 50% of tasks and pass^8 below 25% in retail (paper abstract).

org: Meta (FAIR), Hugging Face and AutoGPT / GenAI (authors Mialon, Fourrier, Swift, Wolf, LeCun, Scialom; affiliations per secondary source, unconfirmed on the abstract page)
tests: Real-world assistant questions that need several steps: web browsing, reading files (PDF, image, audio), reasoning and tool use. Questions are easy for people but hard for AI. Three difficulty levels.
questions: 466 total in the abstract (300 with hidden answers for the leaderboard); the dataset page says 450+; validation set 165 questions (HAL)
format: Open-ended question + optional attached file in, short final answer out
scoring: Exact-match accuracy on the final answer, overall and per level
best_score: 74.55% on the validation set (Claude Sonnet 4.5 in the HAL Generalist scaffold, Princeton HAL, verified); H2O.ai reportedly above 75% on the test set (secondary article, unconfirmed)
best_date: late 2025 (page has no date; HAL updates paused after Oct 2025)
saturated_note: Saturation: Level 1 is near 82% for the top scaffolded agent; overall around 75% so near rather than fully saturated. Launch: GPT-4 with plugins 15% vs humans 92%. Contamination: the dataset is gated and users agree not to reshare it in crawlable form, but it has been public since 2023 so leakage is plausible; I found no measured contamination study. What scores depend on: the scaffold and tools (bare models vs scaffolded agents differ by about 30 points in one secondary article; GPT-5 Mini bare-model 44.8 on an aggregator vs 74.55 with HAL scaffold), validation vs test set, and the judge. HAL notes its cost numbers are overstated by double counting. GAIA is not on the Qwen3.5, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5 or Nemotron pages I read.

org: OpenAI (authors Wei, Sun, Papay, McKinney, Han, Fulford, Chung, Passos, Fedus, Glaese; org per OpenAI page)
tests: How well a browsing agent finds hard-to-find facts on the web. Questions were written backwards from a known answer so they are hard to search but easy to check.
format: Short question in, short single answer out, using a search/browse tool
scoring: Accuracy: the answer is compared to the reference answer by an LLM grader (grader details not on the pages I read)
human_baseline: Human trainers solved 29.2% of problems they tried (367 of 1,255) in 2 hours, and gave an answer matching the reference 86.4% of the time
best_score: 92.5% (Atria Dawn Preview, BenchLM, all rows provider self-reports); 93.6% for Claude Opus 5 in a 10-agent pre-release setup is listed display-only
best_model: Atria Dawn Preview (BenchLM, 2026-10-16); I could not verify this model
saturated_note: Launch: GPT-4o 0.6%, o1 9.9%, Deep Research 51.5% (OpenAI page; Deep Research was trained on BrowseComp-style data). BenchLM flags saturation as active with the top three within 0.8 points. Contamination: real. Anthropic found answers to 9 of 1,266 problems leaked in public web content (at least 20 sources, mostly papers incl. ICLR 2026 submissions) and 2 cases where Opus 4.6 recognized the benchmark and decrypted the answer key (adjusted score 86.57 vs 86.81). What scores depend on: browser/search tools, context management (GLM-5: 62.0 with discard-all vs 75.9 with its hierarchical strategy; Qwen3.5-397B: 69.0 vs 78.6), search budget, number of attempts or agents, and the grader model (GLM-5 used o3-mini). BrowseComp-Plus is a different benchmark with a fixed corpus; do not compare numbers.

org: Salesforce AI Research (authors incl. Ziyang Luo, Caiming Xiong, Junnan Li; org per GitHub)
tests: Agents using real MCP servers (the Model Context Protocol, a standard way to plug tools into a model) on hard real-world tasks in 6 domains: location navigation, repository management, financial analysis, 3D design (Blender), browser automation, web search.
format: Agentic: task + real MCP servers (GitHub, Google Maps, Notion, Blender etc.) in, final output and state checked
scoring: Success rate from three evaluator types: format, static (fixed ground truth) and dynamic (real-time ground truth fetched when answers change)
saturated_note: Launch: GPT-5 43.72%, Grok-4 33.33%, Claude-4.0-Sonnet 29.44% (arXiv abstract). Not saturated: best is under 45%. Contamination: not discussed; dynamic evaluators fetch live ground truth, which limits memorizing. What scores depend on: the agent loop (ReAct one tool per step vs function-call track; GPT-5-Medium 43.72 ReAct vs 41.99 function calls), the tool set and servers (needs external API keys, results can drift with live data), and context length (the paper says context grows quickly). The page text is internally inconsistent (insight text says 43.72 best, tables show higher). Not listed on the model cards I read; the Qwen3.5-397B card lists MCP-Mark and DeepSeek-V4 and GLM-5 list MCPAtlas instead (different benchmarks).

org: ModelScope (Alibaba) (authors Zhiling Luo, Xiaorong Shi, Xuanrui Lin, Jinyang Gao)
tests: Not a test of models: it compares MCP servers (for example Brave, Bing and DuckDuckGo search servers) by running the same model and agent against each one. Tasks: web search, database query, GAIA questions.
questions: unconfirmed (task counts not on pages I fetched)
format: Agentic: same LLM + agent, different MCP server; measure the server
scoring: Task completion accuracy, latency and token use
best_score: 64% (Bing Web Search server, arXiv abstract; a server score, not a model score)
best_model: Bing Web Search MCP server (2025-04 report)
saturated_note: Not a model leaderboard, so saturation and contamination do not really apply (not discussed in sources). Do not confuse with MCP-Universe, MCP-Mark or MCPAtlas. Scores depend on the LLM and agent held fixed, the search backend and network latency. Abstract also says a declarative interface can boost MCP server accuracy substantially.

org: Stanford University and the Laude Institute (Snorkel AI contributed)
tests: Hard, human-verified tasks run by an agent in a Docker terminal (software engineering, sysadmin, security etc.); 16 categories (4 easy, 55 medium, 30 hard).
format: Agentic: instruction + container in; tests check final container state only
scoring: Task resolution rate (all tests of a task must pass); results depend on agent harness and model
human_baseline: None reported (each task has a human-written oracle solution)
best_score: 84.7% (+/-2.1) Terminal-Bench leaderboard (hosted by Snorkel); independent Vals AI best 73.2%
best_model: NexAU-AHE agent + GPT-5.5 (leaderboard entry; whether the run was checked by the maintainers is unconfirmed); Vals AI: GPT 5.5 with Terminus 2 harness (run by Vals, 2026-06-04)
saturated_note: First >50%: Gemini 3 Pro 54.2% with Terminus-2 (as cited in the GLM-5 paper table; original report date about 2025-11, unconfirmed). Claude Opus 4.5 59.3 (Terminus-2) in the same table. Paper abstract (2026-01) says frontier agents were under 65%. Top 10 leaderboard entries span about 7 points with heavily overlapping 95% CIs. Known issues: GLM-5 reports a 'verified' fix of ambiguous task instructions (56.2 -> 60.7 Terminus-2); the authors aimed to keep frontier models under 50% but that no longer holds. Vals AI archived its run citing saturation; Terminal-Bench 4.0 is the successor, so 2.0 scores are not comparable with 4.0. BenchLM: 43 of 45 rows are provider self-reports (GPT-5.5 82%). Reused from the Task 9 card (09-coding-benchmarks/data/benchmarks.csv); not re-researched here. Scaffold dependence: GLM-5 paper reports 56.2 with Terminus-2 and 56.2 with Claude Code on the same model.
